fruits.extendedStory: They feared, so the tale goes, that it would call vengeful spirits down on the city. Tradition names the Temple of Olympian Zeus as the column's source, but Hadrian's Library, close by, is the likelier one. The mosque stood at the heart of the old market, next to its fountain. People knew it as the Mosque of the Lower Fountain. After Greek independence, it hosted a ball for King Otto. The mosque's minaret was pulled down between 1839 and 1843. Today the building is part of the Museum of Modern Greek Culture.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Man fürchtete, so heißt es, es würde rachsüchtige Geister auf die Stadt herabrufen. Die Überlieferung nennt das Olympieion, den Tempel des Zeus, doch wahrscheinlicher stammt die Säule aus der nahen Hadriansbibliothek. Die Moschee stand mitten im alten Markt, neben dessen Brunnen. Man kannte sie als Moschee des Unteren Brunnens. Nach der Unabhängigkeit Griechenlands fand in der Moschee ein Ball für König Otto statt. Ihr Minarett wurde zwischen 1839 und 1843 abgerissen. Heute gehört der Bau zum Museum für moderne griechische Kultur.
localizedExtendedStory.en: They feared, so the tale goes, that it would call vengeful spirits down on the city. Tradition names the Temple of Olympian Zeus as the column's source, but Hadrian's Library, close by, is the likelier one. The mosque stood at the heart of the old market, next to its fountain. People knew it as the Mosque of the Lower Fountain. After Greek independence, it hosted a ball for King Otto. The mosque's minaret was pulled down between 1839 and 1843. Today the building is part of the Museum of Modern Greek Culture.

localizedStory.de: Der Überlieferung nach machte der Erbauer Kalk aus einer Tempelsäule. Die Türken sahen darin ein Sakrileg, heißt es, und er verlor sein Amt.
localizedStory.en: The story goes that the builder made lime from a temple column. The Turks, it is said, called it sacrilege, and he lost his job.

fruits.name: Tzami Tzistaraki
fruits.story: The story goes that the builder made lime from a temple column. The Turks, it is said, called it sacrilege, and he lost his job.

fruits.extendedStory: So the tale goes, the guards' skirt, the foustanella, has 400 pleats that stand for the years of Ottoman rule. The guards are Evzones of the Presidential Guard, posted in front of Parliament. On Sunday mornings the whole guard marches here with a band. The square takes its name from the constitution, Syntagma in Greek, that King Otto had to grant in 1843 after an uprising. Digging the metro station below turned up an ancient sculpture foundry, a Roman bath and the bed of the river Iridanos.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Man erzählt, ihr Rock, die Fustanella, habe 400 Falten, die für die Jahre unter osmanischer Herrschaft stehen. Die Wachen sind Evzonen der Präsidentengarde, aufgestellt vor dem Parlament. Sonntagvormittags marschiert die ganze Garde mit Musikkapelle hierher. Seinen Namen hat der Platz von der Verfassung, griechisch Syntagma, die König Otto 1843 nach einem Aufstand gewähren musste. Beim Bau der U-Bahn-Station darunter fand man eine antike Gießerei für Statuen, ein römisches Bad und das Bett des Flusses Iridanos.
localizedExtendedStory.en: So the tale goes, the guards' skirt, the foustanella, has 400 pleats that stand for the years of Ottoman rule. The guards are Evzones of the Presidential Guard, posted in front of Parliament. On Sunday mornings the whole guard marches here with a band. The square takes its name from the constitution, Syntagma in Greek, that King Otto had to grant in 1843 after an uprising. Digging the metro station below turned up an ancient sculpture foundry, a Roman bath and the bed of the river Iridanos.

localizedStory.de: Oben am Syntagma-Platz bewachen zwei Wachen in weißen Faltenröcken das Grabmal des unbekannten Soldaten. Jede Stunde tauschen sie die Plätze.
localizedStory.en: At the top of Syntagma Square, two guards in pleated white skirts watch over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Every hour, they change places.

fruits.name: Plateia Syntagmatos
fruits.story: At the top of Syntagma Square, two guards in pleated white skirts watch over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Every hour, they change places.

fruits.extendedStory: Into the cathedral's walls went material from 72 demolished churches of Athens. Theophil Hansen drew it for a different spot, on Panepistimiou Street. His plans got the walls up to the lowest windows, and then the money ran out. Dimitrios Zezos took over, and after his death François Boulanger finished it. Sophia of Greece married Juan Carlos, the Spanish heir to the throne, here.

localizedExtendedStory.de: In den Mauern der Kathedrale steckt Baumaterial aus 72 abgerissenen Kirchen Athens. Theophil Hansen plante sie ursprünglich für einen anderen Ort, an der Panepistimiou-Straße. Mit seinen Plänen kamen die Mauern bis zu den unteren Fenstern, dann war das Geld aus. Dimitrios Zezos übernahm, und nach seinem Tod vollendete François Boulanger den Bau. Hier heiratete Sophia von Griechenland den spanischen Thronfolger Juan Carlos.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Into the cathedral's walls went material from 72 demolished churches of Athens. Theophil Hansen drew it for a different spot, on Panepistimiou Street. His plans got the walls up to the lowest windows, and then the money ran out. Dimitrios Zezos took over, and after his death François Boulanger finished it. Sophia of Greece married Juan Carlos, the Spanish heir to the throne, here.

localizedStory.de: Steht ein Großer neben einem Kleinen, heißt es in Athen: wie die Metropolis mit Agios Lefteris. Gemeint sind diese Kathedrale und die winzige Kirche daneben.
localizedStory.en: People say a tall and a short person together look like the Metropolis with Agios Lefteris. Here they are: the cathedral and its tiny neighbour.

fruits.name: Mitropolitikos Naos Athinon
fruits.story: People say a tall and a short person together look like the Metropolis with Agios Lefteris. Here they are: the cathedral and its tiny neighbour.

fruits.extendedStory: The story goes that Zeno came to Athens after a shipwreck and sat down at a bookseller's stall. There, the tale says, he fell in love with philosophy, and later he taught here. In Roman times, the writer Apuleius watched sword swallowers and gymnasts out in front. Inside hung painted panels of the Amazons, the fall of Troy and the battle of Marathon. The painter Polygnotos, Plutarch says, took no fee, out of love for the city. Later, the philosopher Synesius wrote that a Roman governor had taken every picture away.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Sage nach kam Zenon nach einem Schiffbruch nach Athen und setzte sich an den Stand eines Buchhändlers. Dort, so heißt es, verliebte er sich in die Philosophie, und später lehrte er hier. In römischer Zeit sah der Schriftsteller Apuleius vor der Halle Schwertschlucker und Turner. Drinnen hingen einst bemalte Tafeln mit den Amazonen, dem Fall Trojas und der Schlacht von Marathon. Der Maler Polygnot nahm laut Plutarch kein Geld dafür, aus Liebe zur Stadt. Später schrieb der Philosoph Synesios, ein römischer Statthalter habe alle Bilder fortgeschafft.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The story goes that Zeno came to Athens after a shipwreck and sat down at a bookseller's stall. There, the tale says, he fell in love with philosophy, and later he taught here. In Roman times, the writer Apuleius watched sword swallowers and gymnasts out in front. Inside hung painted panels of the Amazons, the fall of Troy and the battle of Marathon. The painter Polygnotos, Plutarch says, took no fee, out of love for the city. Later, the philosopher Synesius wrote that a Roman governor had taken every picture away.

localizedStory.de: In dieser Säulenhalle, der Stoa, lehrte der Philosoph Zenon. Nach ihr nannte man seine Schüler die Stoiker.
localizedStory.en: The philosopher Zeno taught in this colonnade, the stoa. His followers took their name from it, and became known as the Stoics.

fruits.name: Poikili Stoa
fruits.story: The philosopher Zeno taught in this colonnade, the stoa. His followers took their name from it, and became known as the Stoics.

fruits.extendedStory: Every day the fish hall takes in about five to ten tonnes of fresh fish. Much of it comes from islands like Naxos, Paros and Kalymnos. The market takes its name from the Varvakion school that once stood opposite, where the vegetable market is today. Ioannis Varvakis founded that school. He made his fortune fishing the Caspian Sea. He also invented watertight wooden boxes that kept caviar fresh on the long trip by ship.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Jeden Tag kommen etwa fünf bis zehn Tonnen frischen Fisch in die Fischhalle. Vieles davon stammt von Inseln wie Naxos, Paros und Kalymnos. Ihren Namen hat die Markthalle vom Varvakion-Gymnasium, das gegenüber stand, wo heute der Gemüsemarkt ist. Gestiftet hat die Schule Ioannis Varvakis. Reich wurde er mit Fischfang im Kaspischen Meer. Er erfand auch wasserdichte Holzkisten, in denen Kaviar die lange Schiffsreise frisch überstand.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Every day the fish hall takes in about five to ten tonnes of fresh fish. Much of it comes from islands like Naxos, Paros and Kalymnos. The market takes its name from the Varvakion school that once stood opposite, where the vegetable market is today. Ioannis Varvakis founded that school. He made his fortune fishing the Caspian Sea. He also invented watertight wooden boxes that kept caviar fresh on the long trip by ship.

localizedStory.de: Man sagt, diese Halle sei der Bauch von Athen, wie einst die Pariser Markthallen. In der Mitte liegt Fisch, rundum in den Gängen Fleisch.
localizedStory.en: Locals call this market the belly of Athens, like the old halls of Paris. Fish fills the middle hall, meat the lanes round the edge.

fruits.name: Varvakeios Agora
fruits.story: Locals call this market the belly of Athens, like the old halls of Paris. Fish fills the middle hall, meat the lanes round the edge.

fruits.extendedStory: It was a popular joke, and the royal stables really stood where he points. The rider is Theodoros Kolokotronis, a hero of the 1821 Revolution. Queen Amalia founded the house for a Parliament and a Senate. After King Otto was driven out, the Senate was abolished, and Panagiotis Kalkos left its hall out of the plans. Greece's parliament met here until 1935, then moved to the former palace on Syntagma Square, where it still sits. The debating chamber here is preserved unchanged, and the other rooms hold a museum.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das war ein beliebter Witz, und die königlichen Ställe standen wirklich dort, wohin er zeigt. Der Reiter ist Theodoros Kolokotronis, ein Held der Revolution von 1821. Königin Amalia gründete das Haus für Parlament und Senat. Nach der Vertreibung König Ottos wurde der Senat abgeschafft, und Panagiotis Kalkos ließ dessen Saal aus den Plänen weg. Bis 1935 tagte hier das griechische Parlament, dann zog es in den früheren Palast am Syntagma-Platz, wo es bis heute sitzt. Der Plenarsaal hier ist unverändert erhalten, die übrigen Räume gehören zum Museum.
localizedExtendedStory.en: It was a popular joke, and the royal stables really stood where he points. The rider is Theodoros Kolokotronis, a hero of the 1821 Revolution. Queen Amalia founded the house for a Parliament and a Senate. After King Otto was driven out, the Senate was abolished, and Panagiotis Kalkos left its hall out of the plans. Greece's parliament met here until 1935, then moved to the former palace on Syntagma Square, where it still sits. The debating chamber here is preserved unchanged, and the other rooms hold a museum.

localizedStory.de: Der Bronzereiter blickt zum alten Parlament und zeigt weg. Man erzählt, er zeige den Schmeichlern des Königs ihren Platz: die königlichen Ställe.
localizedStory.en: The bronze rider faces the old Parliament but points away. The story goes he was showing the King's flatterers where they belonged: the royal stables.

fruits.name: Ethniko Istoriko Mouseio
fruits.story: The bronze rider faces the old Parliament but points away. The story goes he was showing the King's flatterers where they belonged: the royal stables.

fruits.extendedStory: By 1936, the columnist found it newly planted. The columnist wrote that some Athenians had given it a nickname: Kotzia Square, after Kotzias, the man who remade it. The columnist joked that it was a Kotzaplateia, a whopper of a square. In the end, the Kotzia name went to the square by City Hall. This one kept the name of Alexandros Koumoundouros, a prime minister in the mid-19th century.

localizedExtendedStory.de: 1936 fand der Kolumnist ihn frisch bepflanzt vor. Manche Athener, schrieb der Kolumnist, gaben ihm schon einen Spitznamen: Kotzia-Platz, nach Kotzias, der ihn neu gestaltet hatte. Der Kolumnist spottete, das sei eine Kotzaplateia, ein Riesenplatz. Am Ende ging der Name Kotzia an den Platz beim Rathaus. Dieser hier behielt den Namen von Alexandros Koumoundouros, Ministerpräsident Mitte des 19. Jahrhunderts.
localizedExtendedStory.en: By 1936, the columnist found it newly planted. The columnist wrote that some Athenians had given it a nickname: Kotzia Square, after Kotzias, the man who remade it. The columnist joked that it was a Kotzaplateia, a whopper of a square. In the end, the Kotzia name went to the square by City Hall. This one kept the name of Alexandros Koumoundouros, a prime minister in the mid-19th century.

localizedStory.de: Ein Kolumnist kannte diesen Platz aus seiner Schulzeit als hoffnungslose Sahara. Blies der Wind, legte sich sein Staub wie Londoner Nebel über das Viertel.
localizedStory.en: A columnist remembered this square from school days as a hopeless Sahara. When the wind blew, its dust covered the neighbourhood like a London fog.

fruits.name: Plateia Koumoundourou
fruits.story: A columnist remembered this square from school days as a hopeless Sahara. When the wind blew, its dust covered the neighbourhood like a London fog.

fruits.extendedStory: Two tales tell who built Kapnikarea. One says a princess, and the church is said to have once been called the Princess's Church. The other says its founder collected the kapnikon, the hearth tax, and that is probably where the name comes from. It went up in the third quarter of the 11th century, in the Byzantine style. The bulk of the frescoes inside are by Fotis Kontoglou. He brought the Byzantine way of painting back into modern Greek icons.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Wer die Kapnikarea baute, erzählt man auf zwei Arten. Eine Erzählung nennt eine Prinzessin, und früher, heißt es, hieß die Kirche Prinzessinnenkirche. Die andere sagt, ihr Gründer habe das Kapnikon eingetrieben, die Herdsteuer, und daher komme wohl ihr Name. Erbaut wurde sie im dritten Viertel des 11. Jahrhunderts, im byzantinischen Stil. Den Großteil der Fresken innen malte Fotis Kontoglou. Er brachte die byzantinische Malweise zurück in die moderne griechische Ikonenkunst.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Two tales tell who built Kapnikarea. One says a princess, and the church is said to have once been called the Princess's Church. The other says its founder collected the kapnikon, the hearth tax, and that is probably where the name comes from. It went up in the third quarter of the 11th century, in the Byzantine style. The bulk of the frescoes inside are by Fotis Kontoglou. He brought the Byzantine way of painting back into modern Greek icons.

localizedStory.de: Architekt Klenze wollte die Kirche für die Ermou-Straße abreißen. Ludwig von Bayern überzeugte seinen Sohn, König Otto: Sie ist wichtig. Die Straße weicht aus.
localizedStory.en: Architect Klenze wanted this church gone for Ermou Street. Ludwig of Bavaria persuaded his son, King Otto, it mattered. The street goes round it.

fruits.name: Panagia Kapnikarea
fruits.story: Architect Klenze wanted this church gone for Ermou Street. Ludwig of Bavaria persuaded his son, King Otto, it mattered. The street goes round it.
